newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yield falls to 21.53 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yield falls to 21.53 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs VE6MTMA=RR fell 146 basis points to 21.53 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 50 billion bolivars of 178- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 23.00 percent coupon for a price of 100.66 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 22.99 percent

The bank also sold 15 billion bolivars of 269-day notes VE9MTMA=RR with a 23.66 percent coupon at a price of 100.09 percent, and 15 billion bolivars of 358-day notes VE1YTMA=RR with a 24.33 percent coupon at an average price of 99.94 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 137 basis points to 23.53 percent for the 269-day bills, and 126 basis points to 24.40 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
